blogs.title: When an ‘Adnexal Cyst’ Is a Fibroid: Diagnostic Pitfalls in Pregnancy
blogs.description: Walk through how large, cystic, pedunculated leiomyomas can masquerade as adnexal masses in pregnancy—even on quality ultrasound and MRI. We’ll dissect the sonographic and MRI features that favor degenerating leiomyoma vs decidualized endometrioma, why vascular pedicles and feeding vessels can be hard to visualize as the gravid uterus expands, and how bimanual exam still adds value. Practical pearls for building a structured differential in pregnant patients with atypical pelvic/abdominal cystic masses.

blogs.title: Imaging Strategy for Pelvic Masses in Pregnancy: Ultrasound, Doppler, and Non-Contrast MRI
blogs.description: A pragmatic imaging algorithm for symptomatic or atypical pelvic masses during the second trimester: what ultrasound can and cannot resolve; the role of color Doppler; when to escalate to non-contrast MRI; and safety considerations (field strength, avoiding gadolinium). Case-based tips on interpreting thick-walled cysts with inhomogeneous content, hypertrophied vessels, and uncertain tissue planes, plus how imaging informs operative versus expectant management.

blogs.title: CA-125 in Pregnancy: Red Herring or Helpful Trend?
blogs.description: How to interpret a modestly elevated CA-125 in a pregnant patient with adnexal-appearing masses. We’ll review physiologic trimester-specific ranges, benign conditions that raise CA-125 (endometriosis, leiomyoma, inflammation), and why absolute cutoffs perform poorly in pregnancy. Emphasis on trending values, integrating with imaging and clinical context, and avoiding over-calling malignancy that drives unnecessary intervention.

blogs.title: To Cut or Not to Cut: Second-Trimester Myomectomy for Symptomatic Masses
blogs.description: Decision-making under uncertainty: balancing pain, dyspnea from mass effect, torsion/rupture risk, and oncologic concern against risks of surgery in pregnancy. We’ll outline indications for intervention (e.g., twisted pedunculated myoma, intractable symptoms, infection), choosing laparotomy vs laparoscopy, and strategies to minimize obstetric risk—short operative times, targeted myomectomy (treat the culprit lesion only), hemostasis, and meticulous uterine closure.

blogs.title: Operating with a Passenger: Intraoperative Fetal Monitoring, Anesthesia, and Tocolysis
blogs.description: Operationalizing safe non-obstetric surgery in the second trimester: documenting fetal heart activity before/after (and intermittently during) surgery, anesthesia choices, maternal positioning to optimize ventilation in mass effect, and postoperative monitoring. We’ll examine the evidence and controversies around prophylactic progesterone/tocolysis, antibiotic selection aligned to intercurrent infections, and multidisciplinary communication that preserves pregnancy while treating the mother.

blogs.title: Planning the Delivery Around Big Fibroids: Mapping, Timing, and Route
blogs.description: Using serial ultrasound/MRI to predict labor obstruction and plan delivery. We’ll discuss how size, number, and location (e.g., large posterior lower-segment leiomyoma) influence the likelihood of vaginal birth, indications for scheduled cesarean, and whether to perform concurrent myomectomy. Postpartum regression patterns, counseling on delayed myoma surgery, and aligning maternal preferences with evolving anatomy round out the roadmap.
